'''CNN''' (Cable News Network) is an American cable news channel founded by '''Ted Turner''' in 1980 — the first 24-hour television news network. It is covered in [[Media and Personalities]] as a cable outlet with a long history, and read as corporate media with its own commitments, '''not''' as the neutral standard against which [[Fox News]] is measured.

== The real history ==

CNN invented the format: round-the-clock television news, with the reach to cover a story live anywhere on earth. Its reputation was made in moments of global crisis — most famously the live Gulf War coverage of 1991 — when it was, briefly, the place the world and its governments watched. That first-mover authority is the core of the brand and of why it matters.

== What it is ==

A legacy cable-news operation that has spent much of its later life trying to hold a "centrist" or "straight-news" position between a polarizing competitor on the right and an increasingly partisan environment overall — a position that satisfies few and that has shifted with ownership and ratings pressure. Its anchors and panel formats set a template the whole cable industry copied.

== The strong case ==

CNN built the live-global-news capacity that genuinely served the public in crises, maintained real international bureaus when others cut them, and at its best does serious on-the-ground reporting. The format it pioneered democratized access to breaking news worldwide.

== The weak case ==

It carries the standard corporate-media failures, and this Library is explicit that "centrist" is itself a position, not an absence of one: ratings-driven sensationalism and wall-to-wall coverage of whatever drives engagement, access-journalism deference to power, and — like every legacy outlet — a long institutional history that is far from the neutral baseline its branding implies. The surrounding American press has had to issue its own apologies for a century of coverage (see the record cited in [[SoapBox Oversight]] and the [[White supremacy is media-wide]] framing). Read CNN as one committed institution among several, not as the referee.
